answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the ember check immediately, the relic audit keeps the resolved set and the dawn replay shows exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 76 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 76 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
